TARGET ENGAGEMENT: The trial measured ERK phosphorylation changes by immunohistochemistry H score and plasma concentrations of both dabrafenib and trametinib, indicating target engagement was assessed. However, the primary endpoint (percentage change in p-ERK H score) was not met with no clear numeric result reported. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: The intended biology was inhibition of ERK phosphorylation and MAPK signaling pathway. While p-ERK changes were measured, the results show 'variable p-ERK changes across treatment arms and timepoints' without clear pathway modulation success. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Despite unclear primary biomarker endpoint results, all three arms showed clinical success on ORR (11%, 13%, 11% respectively), suggesting clinical benefit was achieved. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup findings were reported. 5. CONFOUNDERS: The study was terminated early due to slow enrollment and limited viable tissue samples, which likely affected the biomarker analysis but not the clinical efficacy assessment.
